concerns.text: FR-009 mandates a Durbin‑Watson test and Newey‑West standard errors. The original idea never required autocorrelation diagnostics or heteroscedasticity adjustments; these are methodological extensions not justified in the idea and constitute scope over‑reach.

FR-007 introduces censored‑observation handling via a Tobit model. The idea only asked for regression on bounded trajectories and reporting escape probability; it did not specify a censored regression approach, so this adds unrequested functionality.

The 30‑second runtime limit and batch‑processing fallback for trajectories longer than 10 000 steps are engineering constraints not mentioned in the idea. They expand the scope beyond what was requested.
The requirement that the clean baseline be a *vector* of exponents proportional to degrees of freedom adds detail not present in the idea, which only required a scalar asymptotic Lyapunov exponent.

Mandating Benjamini‑Hochberg FDR correction (q ≤ 0.05) and a conditional Tobit model for escape‑probability >5 % are methodological choices absent from the original research question; they represent scope creep.
